formation.title: The Kingdom of Sardinia
formation.text:
The crown of Sardinia sits upon our brow. This island, home to one of Europe's oldest civilizations, now rises as a kingdom in its own right. The ancient Giudicati governed themselves with laws more progressive than any on the continent: the Carta de Logu granted rights to women, enshrined equality before the law, and was written in the people's own tongue. Yet the tides of history have also brought Aragonese ambition, Genoese commerce, and now the calculating vision of the House of Savoy.

Two paths lie before us. We may draw upon the island's deep traditions of self-governance and legal excellence, building a kingdom rooted in the ancient Sardinian way. Or we may embrace the continental vision of the Savoy dynasty, forging Sardinia into a modern military state capable of reshaping the Italian peninsula.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

modifiers.name: Carta de Logu
modifiers.text: The ancient legal code of the Giudicati endures as the foundation of Sardinian governance, granting rights and protections that few in Europe can match.

modifiers.name: Savoyard Ambition
modifiers.text: The House of Savoy transforms Sardinia from an island backwater into the springboard for continental ambition, modernizing the army and bureaucracy.

advances.name: Corona de Logu
advances.text: The corona de logu is the assembly of a judgedom: its prelates, its great men and the curators of its districts. It confirms each new judge, gives its assent to war and treaty, and sits as the highest court of the land. Below it a corona meets in every district to hear the suits of the villages.

event.title: The Carta de Logu
event.text:
In 1392, Eleonora d'Arborea promulgated the Carta de Logu: a legal code of 198 chapters written not in Latin but in Sardinian, the language of the people it governed. It established principles that would not appear elsewhere in Europe for centuries: women could inherit property and refuse marriage, equality before the law was enshrined regardless of birth, and environmental protections governed the use of forests and waterways.

The code proved so effective that when the Crown of Aragon finally conquered the island, they adopted it wholesale. It remained the law of Sardinia until 1827: over four centuries of continuous use, a testament to the wisdom of a woman whom Sardinians still call 'sa mama de su populu,' the mother of the people.

advances.name: Nuragic Heritage
advances.text: Over seven thousand stone towers from the Bronze Age dot the Sardinian landscape, a testament to the island's ancient culture of fortification and territorial defense.

advances.name: Pastoral Heartland
advances.text: For millennia, Sardinia's interior has been the domain of shepherds. The island's wool, cheese, and livestock are the foundation of its economy.

advances.name: Arborean Resistance
advances.text: The Giudicato of Arborea stood as the last bastion of independent Sardinian rule, waging a decades-long war against Aragonese conquest with fierce determination.

advances.name: Coral Riviera
advances.text:
The waters off Alghero yield some of the finest red coral in the Mediterranean, prized from Genoa to Constantinople for its beauty and rarity.

Available in: Silversmiths' Gremio

advances.name: Royal Sea Fortresses
advances.text: The crown of Aragon holds the island from its walled towns on the coast. Alghero, the Castle of Cagliari and Castellaragonese are given new curtain walls and bastions toward the sea, and are garrisoned by the king's own men.

advances.name: Sanluri Legacy
advances.text: The Battle of Sanluri in 1409, where Sardinian independence was lost in a day of terrible bloodshed, remains a defining moment in the island's collective memory.

event.title: The Battle of Sanluri
event.text:
On June 30, 1409, the armies of the Giudicato of Arborea met the forces of the Crown of Aragon at Sanluri, in what would become the last great battle for Sardinian independence. The Arborean army, reinforced by Genoese allies and Sardinian volunteers from across the island, fought with desperate courage against the professional Catalan-Aragonese forces.

The battle was a bloodbath. Thousands fell on both sides, and by day's end, Arborea's military power was broken. The Giudicato lingered for another eleven years (its territories sold to Aragon in 1420), but Sanluri marked the end of independent Sardinia. The memory burns differently depending on who tells the tale: some speak of the fierce Sardinian charge that nearly broke the Aragonese line, others of the stubborn defense that made conquest unbearably costly.

modifiers.name: Arborean Triumph
modifiers.text: The memory of Arborea's defiance inspires our soldiers with unshakeable fighting spirit.

modifiers.name: Sanluri Remembrance
modifiers.text: The bitter lessons of Sanluri harden our defenses. Never again shall an invader take our island cheaply.

advances.name: Silver Mountains
advances.text:
The mines of the Iglesiente around Villa di Chiesa have yielded silver since antiquity. The masters of the royal towns work it into the filigree buttons, chains and reliquaries of the island.

Available in: Silversmiths' Gremio

advances.name: Catalan Legacy
advances.text: Centuries of Catalan-Aragonese rule left a lasting cultural imprint on Sardinia, particularly in Alghero where Catalan is still spoken, bringing Mediterranean trade connections and architectural splendor. The coral boats of Alghero put to sea under the escort of the town's own galleys.

advances.name: Barbagia Refuge
advances.text: The mountainous interior region of Barbagia has resisted every invader from Rome to Aragon. Its rugged terrain and fierce inhabitants make it an unconquerable heartland.

advances.name: Tuna Mattanza
advances.text: The ancient practice of mattanza (the great communal tuna harvest) sustains coastal communities and trains skilled sailors in seamanship and coordinated maritime action. Where the tuna run close inshore a tonnara is set: a maze of nets ending in the chamber of death, with a station on the beach to salt the catch.

advances.name: Sardinian Companies
advances.text: Sardinian soldiers serve in companies across the Mediterranean, gaining a reputation for toughness and endurance that belies their island's modest size.

advances.name: Feudal Reform
advances.text: Attempts to reform the antiquated feudal system imposed by Aragon meet fierce resistance from entrenched barons but gradually strengthen crown authority.

advances.name: Island Fortress
advances.text: Every village of the island keeps horsemen on the militia rolls. When the towers of the coast light their fires, the mounted militia rides for the threatened shore.

advances.name: Pastoral Export
advances.text:
Sardinian pecorino cheese, fine wool, salted hides and cured meats find eager markets across the Mediterranean, establishing the island as a specialist in pastoral goods.

Available in: Pinnetta

advances.name: Royal Pragmatics
advances.text: In 1640 the jurist Francisco de Vico publishes the laws and royal pragmatics of the kingdom in one collection. The scattered orders of two centuries of kings become a single body of law that every court of the island can cite.

advances.name: Supreme Council of Sardinia
advances.text: From 1721 a Supreme Council of Sardinia sits at the court of the island's new Savoyard king. Its regent and councillors review the acts of the viceroy and carry the petitions of the island to the sovereign.

advances.name: Dragoons of Sardinia
advances.text: Raised in 1726 for the service of the island, the Dragoons of Sardinia ride against the bandits of the interior, escort the king's judges, and fight on foot when war comes.

advances.name: New Colonies
advances.text: In 1738 Ligurian coral fishers from Tabarka are settled on the island of San Pietro, where they build the town of Carloforte. Other planted settlements follow on empty coasts, and waste land is brought under the plough.

advances.name: Barracelli Companies
advances.text: Each village swears in a company of barracelli, armed men who guard fields and flocks and answer with their own goods for what is stolen. They know every track of their district and can be called out in a day.

advances.name: The Royal Crown
advances.text: By the Treaty of London the island passes in 1720 to the House of Savoy, which takes from it the title of king. A crown that dukes fought a generation to win ranks its holder among the sovereigns of Europe.

event.title: A Crown Among the Powers
event.text:
For a generation the powers of Europe have passed the island from hand to hand. An English and Dutch fleet took Cagliari for the Habsburg claimant in 1708, Spain seized it back in 1717, and the Treaty of London gave it to the House of Savoy, which took possession in 1720. Whoever wears this crown is a king, and kings are watched.

The island's place among the powers can be kept in two ways: by an army that makes it costly to take, or by envoys who make its holder worth having as a friend.

options.text: Let the army answer for the crown.

modifiers.name: Kingdom in Arms
modifiers.text: The regiments of the kingdom are drilled and kept ready to march, so that no power takes the island cheaply.

options.text: Let the envoys answer for the crown.

modifiers.name: Royal Diplomacy
modifiers.text: The king's envoys sit as equals at the courts of Europe, and old enemies are turned into friends.

advances.name: Code of Charles Felix
advances.text: In 1827 King Charles Felix gives the island a single body of civil and criminal law. It replaces the Carta de Logu after more than four centuries and puts every court of the kingdom under one text.

advances.name: The Carlo Felice Road
advances.text: Between 1822 and 1829 a royal road is built the length of the island, from Cagliari through Oristano and Sassari to Porto Torres. Carts replace pack horses, and the grain, cheese and wine of the interior reach the ports.

advances.name: The Court at Cagliari
advances.text: From 1799 to 1814, with the mainland in French hands, the king and his ministers sit at Cagliari and the envoys of the powers come to them there. In 1804 the Royal Agrarian and Economic Society is founded in the city to study the improvement of the island.

advances.name: Modern Coastal Defense
advances.text: The ancient torre network receives modern artillery batteries and trained gun crews, and half-galleys are kept in commission to patrol between the towers against the last Barbary corsairs.

destiny.name: Sardinian Destiny
destiny.text: The Kingdom of Sardinia has been proclaimed. Whether we honor the island's ancient traditions of self-governance or embrace continental ambition, our path forward begins with a stable realm.

event.title: A Kingdom Proclaimed
event.text:
The crown of Sardinia rests upon our sovereign's brow, and with it comes the weight of centuries. This island has endured Phoenician traders, Roman legions, Vandal raiders, Byzantine governors, and Aragonese overlords, yet through it all, something distinctly Sardinian has survived. Now, for the first time in generations, we stand as masters of our own fate.

The realm is stable. The question is what we shall build upon this foundation.

destiny.name: Crown of the Giudicati
destiny.text: Extend Sardinian sovereignty over Corsica, our sister island across the Strait of Bonifacio, and build a thriving wool trade to fund our island kingdom.

children.text: Wool is produced in the market
Wool is traded in the market

event.title: The Giudicati Restored
event.text:
Across the Strait of Bonifacio, the harbors of Corsica now fly our banner. The two great islands of the Tyrrhenian Sea are united under one crown for the first time since antiquity. Corsican and Sardinian, bound by shared language roots and Mediterranean kinship, together form a formidable island realm.

With Corsican timber supplementing our flocks and the wool trade filling our coffers, the ancient dream of the Giudicati (a Sardinian kingdom governed by its own laws and sustained by its own wealth) begins to take tangible shape.

destiny.name: Laws of the Sea
destiny.text: Establish Sardinia as a Mediterranean trading power by building a Wharf in three of our ports, building our treasury, and ensuring salt flows through our capital markets.

children.text: Salt is produced in the market
Salt is traded in the market

event.title: The Salt Roads Flourish
event.text:
Our harbors bustle with commerce. Sardinian salt, drawn from the great pans of Cagliari and Sassari, travels to every corner of the Mediterranean. New wharves line our ports, and foreign merchants compete for access to our markets.

This prosperity brings choices. We might invest directly in trade infrastructure (warehouses, quays, and merchant fleets) to maximize the flow of goods. Or we might channel our wealth into institutional reform, building the schools and courts that will make our island a model of enlightened governance.

options.text: Fill the warehouses and the coffers.

modifiers.name: Salt and Silver Trade
modifiers.text: Sardinian salt and silver flow through our expanded trade networks, enriching the realm but drawing resources from military upkeep.

options.text: Invest in learning and good governance.

modifiers.name: Institutional Reform
modifiers.text: Progressive institutional reforms modernize our island kingdom, though the bureaucratic burden weighs on wartime efficiency.

destiny.name: Parliament of the Isles
destiny.text: Create an island commonwealth spanning the western Mediterranean by taking the Balearics, achieving great prestige, and founding a Library in Cagliari and in Sassari, the island's two cities of learning.

conditions.text: We own Cagliari and Sassari, and each has a Library

event.title: The Parliament of the Isles
event.text:
From the mountains of Sardinia to the shores of Mallorca, our island commonwealth stretches across the western Mediterranean. The Stamenti of Sardinia, the assemblies of Corsica, and the councils of the Balearics all look to our crown, yet each retains the ancient rights and customs of its people.

We stand at the apex of a new kind of Mediterranean power: not a continental empire built on conquest, but a commonwealth of free peoples bound by law, trade, and mutual respect. How shall we govern this achievement?

modifiers.name: Commonwealth of Free Peoples
modifiers.text: Our island commonwealth governs through consent and shared law, reducing separatism and welcoming diverse peoples under one tolerant crown.

options.text: A beacon of law and learning.

modifiers.name: Beacon of Learning
modifiers.text: Our island realm becomes a center of Mediterranean scholarship, its libraries and courts attracting learned men from every shore.

destiny.name: The Piedmontese Bridge
destiny.text: Cross to the mainland by seizing Turin and Nice, the Savoyard heartland that transforms our island kingdom into a continental power.

event.title: The Bridge to the Mainland
event.text:
Turin has fallen. The ancient capital of the House of Savoy, with its grand piazzas and Alpine backdrop, is ours. And with Nice secured on the Riviera, we command both slopes of the Maritime Alps.

No longer merely an island kingdom, Sardinia-Piedmont now straddles the sea and the continent. The road to Italy lies open before us: through the Po Valley, past the spires of Milan, to whatever destiny our arms can seize.

options.text: From the island to the continent.

destiny.name: Kingdom of Two Crowns
destiny.text: Unite northern Italy under our banner by conquering Milan and Genoa, the twin jewels of Lombardy and Liguria.

event.title: The Lombard Crown
event.text:
Milan and Genoa have bent the knee. The richest city in Italy and the greatest port of the Ligurian coast now swell our treasury and our armies. The Iron Crown of Lombardy (that ancient symbol of Italian kingship) is within our grasp.

With northern Italy secured, our generals debate the next phase. Some advocate seizing the spoils of Lombardy to rebuild and reequip our armies for the final push south. Others counsel patience: consolidate our new crown, build cavalry from Lombard stock, and let our supply lines catch up with our ambitions.

options.text: Press the advantage while they reel.

modifiers.name: Spoils of Lombardy
modifiers.text: The wealth of Lombardy fuels our war machine, with fresh recruits and cheaper reinforcements sustaining the march south.

modifiers.name: Weight of the Iron Crown
modifiers.text: The Iron Crown of Lombardy grants legitimacy but demands consolidation, as new cavalry levies and supply lines strain the treasury.

destiny.name: March on Rome
destiny.text: Complete the unification of Italy by taking Rome and Naples, forging a great peninsular kingdom from the Alps to the Mezzogiorno.

event.title: The Eternal City
event.text:
Rome. The Eternal City. For a thousand years, every power that has claimed Italy has reached for this prize, and now our banners fly above the Tiber. Naples too has fallen, and with it the Mezzogiorno (the sun-baked south that completes our dominion over the peninsula).

From the Alpine passes to the Strait of Messina, from the Adriatic coast to the Tyrrhenian shore, Italy is one. The question now is how this achievement will be remembered: as the work of volunteers in arms and revolutionary fire, or as the work of ministers, secret treaties and the careful management of the great powers.

options.text: By the sword of the volunteers!

modifiers.name: The Volunteers' Sword
modifiers.text: Revolutionary fervor and volunteers in arms forge national unity through direct action, integrating conquered peoples by the force of shared ideals.

options.text: By the pen of the ministers.

modifiers.name: The Ministers' Pen
modifiers.text: Diplomatic mastery and loyal subjects sustain the new Italian state, as statecraft and naval investment project power across the Mediterranean.

units.name: Arborean Militia
units.text: Hardy peasant soldiers from the Giudicato of Arborea, skilled in defensive fighting across Sardinia's hills and mountains.

units.name: Coral Galley
units.text: Fast, maneuverable galleys that patrol the Sardinian coast, protecting coral fishers and merchant ships from pirate raids.

units.name: Dragoons of Sardinia
units.text: Soldiers who ride to the trouble and fight on foot. Steady under fire and quick to act, they keep the king's peace between wars.

units.name: Barracelli
units.text: Sworn watchmen of the villages with long guns. They move fast over country they know and shoot well, and they are not trained to stand a long fight.

units.name: Mounted Militia
units.text: Village horsemen on small island horses, called out by the fires of the coastal towers. They are many and quick to gather, and were never drilled to stand in a line.

units.name: Half-Galley
units.text: A light oared warship of the Sardinian coast guard, quick in a calm and cheap to man. It carries fewer guns than a galley and was among the last of its kind kept by any navy.

buildings.name: Curia Regni
buildings.text: The court of a judgedom, where the corona de logu sits in judgement and the law of the island is administered with a care rare in medieval Europe.

buildings.name: Pinnetta
buildings.text: Traditional Sardinian stone-and-thatch pastoral shelters, serving as the nucleus of the island's thriving sheep and wool economy.

children.text: The location's raw material is Wool
The location's raw material is Livestock

buildings.name: Sea Bastion
buildings.text: A bastion and curtain wall on the seaward side of a coastal town, with a guard of soldiers and a watch over the harbour.

buildings.name: Silversmiths' Gremio
buildings.text: The sworn guild of the silversmiths in a royal town, founded on the Catalan model with its own statutes, patron saint and chapel. Its masters work silver and coral.

buildings.name: Tonnara
buildings.text: A fixed tuna trap and its station on the beach. The nets are set each spring where the tuna pass, and the shore yields far more fish than the boats alone ever took from the run.

where.text: The location's raw material is Fish

buildings.name: Palazzo degli Stamenti
buildings.text: The grand parliamentary palace of the island commonwealth, where elected representatives from Sardinia, Corsica, and the Balearics deliberate the laws that govern a free Mediterranean people.

buildings.name: Palazzo Madama
buildings.text: The seat of the kingdom's senate in Turin. This Roman gate turned baroque palace stands for the change of an island kingdom into the government of a united Italy.

list.name: Carta de Logu
list.text: Eleonora of Arborea promulgated the Carta de Logu in 1392, a 198-chapter code in the Sardinian vernacular, so that those it governed might read it. Women could inherit and refuse marriage; forests and waterways were protected from over-exploitation; the accused could summon ten witnesses; torture was forbidden against those of unblemished reputation. The Aragonese conquerors adopted the code wholesale, and it remained Sardinia's law until Charles Felix's 1827 codification finally superseded it.

list.name: Prime Voci
list.text: Each of the three estates of the kingdom has a first voice. The archbishop of Cagliari speaks for the clergy, the marquis of Laconi for the barons, and the first juror of Cagliari for the royal towns. The king calls a parliament about once in ten years. Between the sessions the first voices summon their estates, carry grievances to the viceroy and see that the grant voted to the crown is levied as it was agreed.

list.name: Curatoria System
list.text: Inherited by the Giudicati from the late Byzantine theme structure, the curatoria divided each judicate into self-sufficient districts (thirteen in Cagliari alone), each overseen by a curator who answered to the iudike rather than to feudal overlords. Land allocation, military levy and local justice ran through these crown appointees. Even after the Aragonese imposed feudal tenures the curatorie persisted as encontradas, keeping royal jurisdiction running parallel to baronial courts.

list.name: Viceregal Court of Cagliari
list.text: From 1325 the Aragonese ruled Sardinia through a viceroy seated at Cagliari, holding the audiencia, the royal patrimony and the high judiciary on behalf of an absentee king. Tridentine viceroys like Cardona and Moncada centralised the tax-farms and pressed Castilian fueros against local custom. The institution outlasted Aragon, Spain and the Austrian interlude, and in honest hands it ran the realm; in venal hands it became proverbial for sale of office and bribery.

list.name: Royal Salt Monopoly
list.text: The salt pans of Molentargius outside Cagliari and the Sassari salines have fed Mediterranean markets since antiquity, but it was the Spanish crown that codified the regalia salis as a royal monopoly in the sixteenth century. Crown contractors shipped the salt under the gabella, the carruba paid in kind: when honestly farmed it built galleys; when farmed out to courtiers it bred smuggling, peasant unrest, and the great salt-revolts that shook eighteenth-century Sardinia.
